claim: NOT9B is an Arabidopsis homologue of human CNOT9.
source: NOT9B, an Arabidopsis homologue of human CNOT9, is a component of the CCR4-NOT complex
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: NOT9B is a component of the CCR4-NOT complex.
source: NOT9B, an Arabidopsis homologue of human CNOT9, is a component of the CCR4-NOT complex
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by co-immunoprecipitation and Y2H data showing interaction with NOT1 (Figure 3).

claim: NOT9B acts as a negative regulator of phyA-specific light signalling when bound to NOT1.
source: NOT9B, an Arabidopsis homologue of human CNOT9, is a component of the CCR4-NOT complex, and acts as negative regulator of phyA-specific light signalling when bound to NOT1, the scaffold protein of the complex.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by phenotypic analysis of not9b mutants and NOT9Box lines showing altered responses to far-red light (Figure 2).

claim: Light-activated phyA interacts with NOT9B.
source: Light-activated phyA interacts with and displaces NOT9B from NOT1
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by Y2H, CoIP, and FRET-FLIM experiments (Figure 1).

claim: Light-activated phyA displaces NOT9B from NOT1.
source: Light-activated phyA interacts with and displaces NOT9B from NOT1, suggesting a potential mechanism for light signalling through CCR4-NOT.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by Y3H competition assays and CoIP experiments (Figure 6).

claim: ARGONAUTE 1 associates with NOT9B.
source: ARGONAUTE 1 and proteins involved in splicing associate with NOT9B
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by AP-MS and CoIP data (Figure 7).

claim: Proteins involved in splicing associate with NOT9B.
source: ARGONAUTE 1 and proteins involved in splicing associate with NOT9B
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by AP-MS data (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).

claim: NOT9B is required for specific phyA-dependent alternative splicing events.
source: we show that NOT9B is required for specific phyA-dependent alternative splicing events.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by analysis of MYBD splicing patterns in not9b mutants (Figure 8).

claim: NOT9B associates with nuclear localised ARGONAUTE 1.
source: Furthermore, association with nuclear localised ARGONAUTE 1 raises the possibility that NOT9B and CCR4-NOT are involved in phyA-modulated gene expression.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by CoIP experiments showing association of NOT9B with AGO1 in nuclear-localized NOT9B lines (Figure 7B).

claim: NOT9B and CCR4-NOT may be involved in phyA-modulated gene expression.
source: Furthermore, association with nuclear localised ARGONAUTE 1 raises the possibility that NOT9B and CCR4-NOT are involved in phyA-modulated gene expression.
evidence: The claim is presented as a possibility based on the association of NOT9B with nuclear AGO1.

claim: Phytochromes are receptors for red and far-red light.
source: Phytochromes are receptors for R and FR light.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge cited in the introduction.

claim: Phytochromes are synthesised in the inactive Pr state and convert to the physiologically active Pfr state upon absorbing light.
source: They are synthesised in the inactive Pr state and convert to the physiologically active Pfr state upon absorbing light (Legris et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: PhyA and phyB are the primary phytochromes in seed plants.
source: PhyA and phyB are the primary phytochromes in seed plants.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge cited in the introduction.

claim: PhyB has a dominant function as red light receptor.
source: PhyB has a dominant function as R light receptor, while responses induced by FR light depend on phyA (Legris et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Responses induced by far-red light depend on phyA.
source: PhyB has a dominant function as R light receptor, while responses induced by FR light depend on phyA (Legris et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Phytochromes are located to the cytosol in the inactive state and translocate into the nucleus upon conversion to the active Pfr state.
source: Phytochromes are located to the cytosol in the inactive state and translocate into the nucleus upon conversion to the active Pfr state (Klose et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: NOT9B interacts with phyA in yeast-two-hybrid assays irrespective of whether phyA is in the active Pfr or inactive Pr state.

claim: The N-terminal 406 amino acids of phyA are sufficient for binding NOT9B.

claim: NOT9C does not interact with phyA in the Y2H system under high stringency conditions.

source: None of the NOT1 fragments competed with FHY1 for binding to phyA, suggesting that co-expression of NOT1 does not generally interfere with interaction of phyA and phyA-binding proteins (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Y3H data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Co-expression of HA-NOT1 M clearly reduced growth of cells expressing the Y2H pair HA-AD-NOT9B/phyA-LUC-BD but had only a minor effect on HA-AD-NOT9B and phyA-LUC-BD protein levels.
source: Co-expression of HA-NOT1 M clearly reduced growth of cells expressing the Y2H pair HA-AD-NOT9B/phyA-LUC-BD but had only a minor effect on HA-AD-NOT9B and phyA-LUC-BD protein levels (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Y3H and immunoblot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Co-expression of FLAG-myc-mCherry-NLS-NOT1 M almost fully abolished assembly of NOT9B into photobodies whilst not affecting phyA photobody formation in tobacco leaves.
source: In contrast, co-expression of FLAG-myc-mCherry-NLS-NOT1 M, which includes the NOT9B binding site of NOT1, almost fully abolished assembly of NOT9B into photobodies whilst not affecting phyA photobody formation.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: FLAG-myc-mCherry-NLS-NOT1 M co-purified with HA-YFP-NOT9B in CoIPs.
source: FLAG-myc-mCherry-NLS-NOT1 M co-purified with HA-YFP-NOT9B in CoIPs (Figure 6D)
evidence: The claim is supported by CoIP data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The amount of phyA Pfr co-precipitating with HA-YFP-NOT9B appeared to be lower in CoIPs from seedlings co-expressing FLAG-myc-mCherry-NLS-NOT1 M than from seedlings not expressing NOT1 M.
source: Interestingly, the amount of phyA Pfr co-precipitating with HA-YFP-NOT9B appeared to be lower in CoIPs from seedlings co-expressing FLAG-myc-mCherry-NLS-NOT1 M than from seedlings not expressing NOT1 M (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by CoIP data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Quantification of three independent CoIP experiments showed that the amount of phyA bound to NOT9B is significantly reduced when NOT1 M is coexpressed.
source: Quantification of three independent CoIP experiments analysed on the same membrane showed that the amount of phyA bound to NOT9B is significantly reduced when NOT1 M is coexpressed (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantified CoIP data shown in Figure 6E,F.

claim: Binding of phyA and NOT1 to NOT9B is mutually exclusive and they compete for binding NOT9B in planta.
source: This finding supports the idea that binding of phyA and NOT1 to NOT9B is mutually exclusive and they compete for binding NOT9B in planta.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Y3H and CoIP competition data.

claim: Levels of phyA are several orders of magnitude higher than the levels of NOT9B.
source: Quantification of the luciferase signal showed that levels of phyA are several orders of magnitude higher than the levels of NOT9B (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase imaging data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claim: CCR4-NOT complexes containing NOT9B (CCR4-NOTNOT9B) repress phyA signalling.
source: Consequently, based on the phenotype of not9b mutants and NOT9Box lines, we propose that CCR4-NOT complexes containing NOT9B (CCR4-NOTNOT9B) repress phyA signalling.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the phenotypic data.

claim: In seedlings exposed to FR light, phyA is transported into the nucleus and competition for binding NOT9B could then displace NOT9B from CCR4-NOTNOT9B, thereby relieving repression of light signalling.
source: In seedlings exposed to FR light, phyA is transported into the nucleus and competition for binding NOT9B could then displace NOT9B from CCR4-NOTNOT9B (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 3), thereby relieving repression of light signalling.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the competition data and phenotypic observations.

claim: The negative effect of NOT9Box on both inhibition of hypocotyl growth in FR light and expression of FR light-induced genes such as EARLY LIGHT INUDCIBLE PROTEIN 1 and 2 (EPLI1/2) and CHS is partially suppressed by co-expression of FLAG-myc-mCherry-NLS-NOT1 M without affecting NOT9B protein levels.
source: In line with this reasoning, the negative effect of NOT9Box on both inhibition of hypocotyl growth in FR light and expression of FR light-induced genes such as EARLY LIGHT INUDCIBLE PROTEIN 1 and 2 (EPLI1/2) and CHS (Harari-Steinberg et al., 2001; Zhou et al., 2005) is partially suppressed by co-expression of FLAG-myc-mCherry-NLS-NOT1 M without affecting NOT9B protein levels (Figure 6G–I, Figure 6—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by hypocotyl length measurements and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6G–I and Figure 6—figure supplement 5.

claim: Silver staining of GFP-trap purified proteins revealed several proteins co-precipitating with HA-YFP-NOT9B but not with YFP-HA.
source: Silver staining of GFP-trap purified proteins revealed several proteins co-precipitating with HA-YFP-NOT9B but not with YFP-HA (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by silver staining data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: By MS-MS, 450 proteins were identified that are only present in the HA-YFP-NOT9B eluate fraction.
source: By MS-MS we identified 450 proteins that are only present in the HA-YFP-NOT9B eluate fraction (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by AP-MS data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The NOT9B interactome includes the known NOT9B interactors NOT1 and phyA, and most components of the CCR4-NOT complex.
source: This includes the known NOT9B interactors NOT1 and phyA, and most components of the CCR4-NOT complex.
evidence: The claim is supported by AP-MS data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: NOT9A and NOT9C were not found among NOT9B-associated proteins in AP-MS.
source: We did not find NOT9A, the closest homologue of NOT9B, and the more distantly related NOT9C.
evidence: The claim is based on the absence of NOT9A and NOT9C in the AP-MS data.

claim: AGO1 and proteins with a function in miRNA biogenesis and/or splicing were among NOT9B-associated proteins.
source: Interestingly, AGO1 and proteins with a function in miRNA biogenesis and/or splicing were among NOT9B-associated proteins.
evidence: The claim is supported by AP-MS data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Highly enriched GO terms among NOT9B-associated proteins were rRNA binding, mRNA binding, RNA binding, and translation elongation factor activity.
source: Highly enriched GO terms among NOT9B-associated proteins were rRNA binding, mRNA binding, RNA binding, and translation elongation factor activity (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: The claim is supported by GO term analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: There is no evidence for direct interaction of NOT9B and AGO1 in Y2H assays.
source: We did not find any evidence for direct interaction of NOT9B and AGO1 in Y2H assays (Figure 7—figure supplement 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by Y2H data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Endogenous AGO1 could be co-precipitated with HA-YFP-NOT9B.
source: but could co-precipitate endogenous AGO1 with HA-YFP-NOT9B
evidence: The claim is supported by CoIP data shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: HA-YFP-NOT9B was found associated with endogenous AGO1 in CoIPs with αAGO1 antibodies.
source: and vice versa found HA-YFP-NOT9B associated with endogenous AGO1 in CoIPs with αAGO1 antibodies (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by CoIP data shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: HA-YFP-NOT9B and AGO1-CFP colocalise in p-bodies of transiently transformed tobacco leaves.
source: We also observed colocalisation of HA-YFP-NOT9B and AGO1-CFP in p-bodies of transiently transformed tobacco leaves (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: AGO1 and NOT9B are in complex but possibly do not directly interact.
source: Overall, AP-MS and CoIP data show that AGO1 and NOT9B are in complex but possibly do not directly interact.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the CoIP data showing association but Y2H data showing no direct interaction.

claim: Hypocotyl growth at intermediate light intensities is reduced in weak, viable ago1 mutants (e.g. ago1-33, ago1-34, and ago1-35) compared to the wildtype.
source: Sorin et al., 2005 have shown that hypocotyl growth at intermediate light intensities is reduced in weak, viable ago1 mutants (e.g. ago1-33, ago1-34, and ago1-35) compared to the wildtype.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The ago1-27 mutant has only slightly shorter hypocotyls than the wildtype in the dark but is hypersensitive to FR light over a wide range of fluence rates.
source: The ago1-27 mutant has only slightly shorter hypocotyls than the wildtype in the dark but is hypersensitive to FR light over a wide range of fluence rates (Figure 7C, Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by hypocotyl length measurements shown in Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 3.

claim: Anthocyanin levels are increased in ago1-27 exposed to FR light, whereas there is no significant difference in the dark and in B light.
source: In addition anthocyanin levels are increased in ago1-27 exposed to FR light, whereas there is no significant difference in the dark and in B light (Figure 7D).
evidence: The claim is supported by anthocyanin quantification data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Cotyledon unfolding is partially impaired in the ago1-27 and the not9b-1 mutants.
source: Cotyledon unfolding is typically enhanced by light but we found that this response is partially impaired in the ago1-27 and the not9b-1 mutants (Figure 7E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by cotyledon opening measurements shown in Figure 7E,F.

claim: The NOT9Box line is also impaired in proper cotyledon unfolding in FR light.
source: Interestingly, the NOT9Box line is also impaired in proper cotyledon unfolding in FR light (Figure 7E,F)
evidence: The claim is supported by cotyledon opening measurements shown in Figure 7E,F.

claim: MYBD is a MYB-related transcription factor that promotes anthocyanin biosynthesis downstream of HY5.
source: MYBD is a MYB-related transcription factor that promotes anthocyanin biosynthesis downstream of HY5 (Nguyen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: MYBD is regulated by alternative splicing; splice variant MYBD.1 encodes a functional protein, while MYBD.2 has a premature stop codon due to intron retention.
source: MYBD is regulated by alternative splicing; splice variant MYBD.1 encodes a functional protein, while MYBD.2 has a premature stop codon due to intron retention (Figure 8A; Hartmann et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation and schematic shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The ratio of MYBD.2/.1 is strongly reduced upon R or FR light treatment.
source: The ratio of MYBD.2/.1 is strongly reduced upon R or FR light treatment, meaning that light shifts the MYBD.2/.1 ratio toward the splice variant that codes for functional MYBD and thereby promotes anthocyanin biosynthesis (Hartmann et al., 2016; Nguyen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: phyA is required for the response of MYBD.2/.1 ratio to FR light.
source: We found that phyA is required for this response to FR light (Figure 8B)
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The MYBD.2/.1 ratio in dark-grown not9b-2 seedlings is similar to wildtype seedlings treated with FR light.
source: and that the MYBD.2/.1 ratio in dark-grown not9b-2 seedlings is similar to wildtype seedlings treated with FR light (Figure 8C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: NOT9B is essential to suppress the shift of the MYBD.2/.1 ratio toward the physiologically active splice variant in etiolated seedlings and FR light perceived by phyA removes this negative regulation.
source: Thus, NOT9B is essential to suppress the shift of the MYBD.2/.1 ratio toward the physiologically active splice variant in etiolated seedlings and FR light perceived by phyA removes this negative regulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the MYBD splicing data in not9b mutants.

claim: Seedlings lacking functional NOT9B do not have an obvious constitutively photomorphogenic (cop) phenotype.
source: Seedlings lacking functional NOT9B do not have an obvious constitutively photomorphogenic (cop) phenotype (Figures 2D and 7E, Figure 2—figure supplement 3A)
evidence: The claim is based on phenotypic observations shown in Figures 2D and 7E, Figure 2—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The splicing pattern of MYBD in etiolated not9-2 resembles the pattern in wildtype seedlings exposed to light.
source: but the splicing pattern of MYBD in etiolated not9-2 resembles the pattern in wildtype seedlings exposed to light (Figure 8C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Expression of EPR1, ELIP1, and ELIP2 was increased in dark-grown not9b-2 seedlings compared to the wildtype.
source: Expression of EPR1, ELIP1, and ELIP2 was increased in dark-grown not9b-2 seedlings compared to the wildtype, supporting the concept that not9b mutant seedlings have a partial cop phenotype at the molecular level (Figure 9A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: When exposed to FR light for 1 hr, EPR1, ELIP1, and ELIP2 transcript levels are similar in not9b-2 and wildtype seedlings.
source: When exposed to FR light for 1 hr, EPR1, ELIP1, and ELIP2 transcript levels are similar in not9b-2 and wildtype seedlings.
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Expression of EPR1 and ELIP1 was also increased in dark-grown NOT9Box seedlings, although not to the same extent as in not9b-2.
source: Expression of EPR1 and ELIP1 was also increased in dark-grown NOT9Box seedlings, although not to the same extent as in not9b-2.
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 9A.
